The city

A mouse is optional: click the view to look with it, or leave it alone and use the keys. The supervisory console on the north wall of the control room carries every setting this page has, and two it does not — the number of vehicles in town, and how hard the safety layer tries.

The town is held at night at every hour. A streetlight's brightness is the voltage at its bus, and daylight would swallow the difference between a healthy street and a browned-out one.

Set Picture to Full quality before recording. Sandbox controls unlock after the six stages, or immediately from the button under the fleet slider.

    Stated objectives

    Eight objectives, each tied to the stage that teaches it. “Reached” means the material was presented, not that it was understood. Only a pre/post assessment establishes that.

    #ObjectiveTaught inStatus

    Run comparison

    Safety on one axis, service on the other. Every run you finish leaves a dot. A comparison carrying only the first column cannot separate a good controller from one that does nothing. Your own runs are scored against the same 287-vehicle fleet the engine uses.

    RunViolation rateDrivers servedLine losses

    The feeder, in text

    Every bus, live, updating with the day — the same data the mimic board carries. The Go to buttons move you around the city without a mouse.

    The procurement shortlist

    The table from stage six, with the deciding column restored. Uncoordinated charging is not on the list because nobody procures it. Figures are for the weak feeder and follow the feeder switch above.

    ControllerViolation rateDrivers servedLine lossesNet costProvenance

    Verification

    The city runs the same backward/forward sweep as the offline engine. On load it re-solves every recorded control step and compares the two, so the numbers on the meters are checked rather than trusted. Two of the four candidates are reference implementations; their figures are provisional and marked as such everywhere they appear.
